ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-029", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: auth-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 11:42 UTC)
Alerting service: auth
Alert time: 2026-05-08T11:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-05-08T10:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T13:00:00Z

Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 15.91 after (124.8 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:10:00Z = 0.1 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z = 15.86 (first point after the change); 2026-05-08T11:45:00Z = 16.09 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:30:00Z = 16.01 (last).

Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z = 0 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:30:00Z = 0 (last).

Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-08T12:30:00Z", "metric": "request_rate_rps", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-05-08T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Verify request rate and traffic spike for auth service around the incident time.)
  Result: M-008: Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 452.67 before, 1809.39 after (162.1 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-008] auth.request_rate_rps from 2026-05-08T11:00:00Z to 2026-05-08T12:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=441.11 max=1832.66 mean=1238.14 last=1826.48; mean=1238.14. Change detected at 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z: mean 452.67 before, 1809.39 after (162.1 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-08T11:10:00Z = 441.11 (lowest); 2026-05-08T11:40:00Z = 1813.3 (first point after the change); 2026-05-08T12:05:00Z = 1832.66 (peak); 2026-05-08T12:30:00Z = 1826.48 (last).
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "traffic spike rate limit load shedding mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for handling traffic spikes and rate limiting issues.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-09-5 (similarity 0.62).
  [R-09-5] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Mitigation (similarity 0.62): Tighten limits on the heaviest caller, raise the ceiling on automatic scaling, and turn away non-essential traffic first. Block abusive sources at the edge. If a client is retrying aggressively, contact whoever owns that client and ask them to back off.
  [R-09-7] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Escalation (similarity 0.60): Call the platform team to raise capacity limits quickly. Tell the business owner about any planned event that nobody mentioned, so capacity can be planned ahead next time. Ask them whether any other region has spare room to take some of the load.
  [R-09-3] Traffic spike and rate limiting - How to confirm (similarity 0.58): Compare the incoming volume with a normal day at this time. If it is several times higher and the machines are busy, this is demand and not a fault. Check whether the automatic scaling has already used up its allowance, and whether one caller accounts for most of the load.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: Metrics show request rate quadrupled at 11:40 UTC, matching log warnings of rate limit breaches, maxed out replicas, and load shedding. (evidence: M-005, M-008, L-0278, L-0279, L-0281)
- downstream_timeout: Logs show 502/503 errors and high durations associated with upstream/cart API calls under heavy load. (evidence: L-0280, L-0287, L-0294)
